## 2. Scope and study basis

**Scope.** The tanker loading procedure at Gantry 2, Site-X. The start/end boundaries of the procedure (e.g. from tanker arrival and positioning through connection, transfer, disconnection, and release) and the product or products handled at Gantry 2 were not stated — **[GAP G1]**; both must be confirmed against the SOP at the reconvened session before the question set is finalised.

**Source documents.** The only input available to this register is the workshop answer extract reproduced at W1. The loading SOP, a P&ID or gantry sketch, and any prior study were not supplied — **[GAP G2]** (Action A2).

**Baseline safeguards for the scope.** Beyond the two safeguards the team recorded against W1, no scope-wide baseline of existing safeguards was recorded — **[GAP G9]**.

**Site context recorded by the team.** 12 recordable injuries this period. This is an aggregate figure; categories containing fewer than 5 individuals are aggregated (with secondary suppression) and no small cell is published or derivable from this register.

## 4. Method

The What-If method structures a systematic sweep of "What if …?" prompts across the bounded scope, following the structured-study discipline of KB-STD-IEC-61882 (the discipline What-If shares with HAZOP, applied in lighter form to procedures and simpler systems). For each question, the **team** supplies the hazard/consequence, the existing safeguards, a risk rank against the agreed matrix, and any recommendation; the register records what the team supplies and records **[GAP]** where the team has not yet answered. Safeguards are ranked against the hierarchy of controls (KB-SNIP-HOC); recommendations are tracked to closure in the actions register (§7). No consequence, safeguard, rank, or recommendation in this register originates anywhere other than the team.

**Question seeds applied:** loss of utility · wrong sequence · wrong material or quantity · human error or omission · equipment failure · external event · start-up / shutdown / abnormal operation.

## 6. Hierarchy-of-controls review of recorded safeguards

Per KB-SNIP-HOC, the safeguards the team recorded are ranked as follows:

| Safeguard (as recorded) | Hierarchy level | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Keyed dedicated connections (W1) | Engineering | Physical prevention of cross-connection |
| Product-verification interlock (W1) | Engineering | Engineered verification before transfer |

**Review.** The recorded set for W1 sits at the engineering level; it is **not** an administrative/PPE-only set, so no lower-order-only flag is raised for this line. Whether higher-order options (elimination or substitution) are feasible for the wrong-product line, and whether supporting administrative layers (e.g. procedural verification steps) exist alongside the engineered safeguards, has not been recorded by the team — carried within **[GAP G6/G9]** for the reconvened session. No safeguards are recorded for W2–W12.

## 9. Limitations and competent-person review

This register is **decision-support only**. It structures the What-If question set and records the team's analysis; it does not perform the study, and in its current state it is explicitly **not** a completed hazard study (see banner). A competent person must review this output — and the reconvened full team must answer, risk-rank, and sign off every line, and track every action to closure — before it is relied on for any operational, engineering, or compliance decision. It is not legal advice.
